key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 AI found the buried killer risk (TianTech capacity-first clause + single congested lane + zero buffer) by line-by-line reading in WHY and reached the permanent channel-displacement consequence only at REVIEW, while the human back-cast got both in-frame; the v6 routed run executes the pre-mortem as a first-class pass with a completion contract — failure assumed first, unsupported causes discarded, causes LxI-ranked (capacity conflict = killer, displacement = critical), mitigation per top cause altering the commitment (T+6/T+10 gates) — and the m003/m019 gates add 7 ranked failure categories and a baseline-risk line. The v6 AI additionally quantified what the human left at High/Med ranks: capacity-conflict likelihood 10/35/60% with a threshold flip at the T+6 media lock.
learning_signal: For guarantee/adversarial commitment decisions, the pre-mortem completion contract (assume-failure back-cast with an evidence-discard rule, LxI ranking, top-1 mitigation that changes the commitment itself, second-order consequence named in-frame, likelihood range per dominant risk) converts 'risk found by reading order luck' into 'risk found by construction' — the v5 AI's own AAR conceded the risk surfaced 'not because the task asked what happened'; the routed pass makes the question mandatory before any commitment is evaluated.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m020 pass as a standing first-class module for decide/guarantee/adversarial signatures with the likelihood-range and threshold-flip additions (tie the flip to a contractual calendar point, here the T+6 media lock); pair it permanently with the m003 inversion gate (never/always reframing) and the m019 baseline-risk-first line; require the packet's risks block to name a second-order consequence of the failure state for every launch-commitment decision.

key_gap: vs baseline: the strict human pre-mortem manufactured a 15-item unranked catastrophe list (venue fire, wifi, food poisoning, hurricanes) for a plan with an 11-run success streak, runbook, and insurance — mitigations either duplicated existing coverage (changed nothing) or escalated to deferral (paralysis) — and never analyzed the actual decision (ticketing adoption); the one genuine risk (migration integrity) was buried at equal weight among fifteen. The routed dual-run (m011 systems scan vs delta-scoped pre-mortem, synthesized) classified the plan unchanged-vs-delta by base rate, discarded the insured generic causes under the evidence rule, capped the pass at 3 LxI-ranked delta risks, and committed adopt-with-gated-rollout (rehearsal gate + numeric criteria + 48h rollback) on a tempo deadline.
learning_signal: The pre-mortem's power is conditional on base rates: 'assume failure' manufactures failure modes when applied to unchanged, historically successful elements — unranked causes whose mitigations duplicate existing coverage or demand escalation. The corrective discipline is the delta-only contract: enumerate causes only for changed elements, discard any cause without scenario-supporting evidence, cap at ~5, rank by likelihood x impact, and end in a decision with a checkpoint/rollback rule — plus tempo-commit at DO so the decision week is not lost.
suggested_improvement: At META/WHAT, classify plan elements as 'unchanged + historically successful' (take as given; runbook/insurance are the existing mitigations) vs 'delta' (the only risk surface) before any risk pass; wire the evidence-discard rule and the <=5 cap into the m020 module contract as gate checks; dual-route m011+m020 on decide/maximize signatures with divergence resolution, and require the m020 pass to terminate in a committed decision with a rollback rule, never a list.
